newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse closes with record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse closes with record turnover.

text.p: Bucharest stock exchange turnover hit a record high of 25.9 billion lei in turnover on Wednesday with six special deals in two first-tier high-caps, which traders said involved foreign interest.
"Foreign buying remained strong, still focusing on the first tier," said a trader. "Special deals were the order of the day and they were struck by foreigners."

Fertiliser maker Azomures had three special trades -- deals struck outside the market and reported to the exchange later -- worth around five billion lei, while Oltchim chemical plant also had three such deals amounting to some seven billion lei.

Azomures closed 50 lei weaker at 3,800, with traders saying the high-cap lost in late trading. "There was profit-taking late in the session," one said. Oltchim gained 200 lei to close at 3,500 under the impact of the special deals, brokers said.
The turnover level on Tuesday was 17.7 billion lei. The previous all-time high, set in late May, was 25.7 billion lei.

Overall volume increased to 6.9 million shares from 4.6 million on Tuesday, while average prices drifted sideways after the recent bull run in what traders said might be the start of a downward market correction to follow in the next few days.
The average prices of 13 stocks climbed, 10 drifted lower and five stayed flat. Ten companies had no trade and two were suspended.

Two unofficial indices, the VAB and the BIG, based on average prices and capitalisation, slipped by 0.7 and 0.3 percent respectively from Tuesday. The BIG first-tier index was 0.97 percent down at 4,495.4 points.
Three of the other four stocks in the first section closed lower, while Antibiotice pharmaceuticals gained 600 lei to end at 5,700.
Policolor dye maker was most heavily traded on the second tier, with 1.9 billion lei in turnover. It closed 100 lei weaker at 5,750.
Compa vehicle parts maker was to join the market on Thursday with its shares trading on the main floor, a bourse official said.
